subject: Demo request: Dedicated throughput/latency evaluation — SequenceLabs
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sequencelabs.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Cc: team@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interested in Dedicated capacity demo (high QPS/low latency)

Hi Redwood team,

We just completed the self-signup and are evaluating Dedicated deployments for a production inference path. A couple quick facts about our workload:
- Peak sustained QPS target: 300 requests/sec for a 512-token average response
- 95th percentile latency target: under 120ms (tail is important for UX)
- Model: open-weights Llama variant (we'll share the model id once we sign NDA)

Can we book a walkthrough that focuses strictly on Dedicated capacity sizing, autoscale behavior, and the fallback behavior when capacity is constrained? If possible we want someone from infra/engineering on the call.

I attached a quick spreadsheet with sample traffic shape.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of ML Engineering
SequenceLabs

Attachment: seq-capacity-specs.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sequencelabs.com>
Cc: avery_johnson@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Dedicated capacity demo (high QPS/low latency)

Hi Alex — welcome and thanks for the details, this is exactly the kind of intake we prefer.

Quick answers and next steps:
- We can focus the walkthrough on Dedicated sizing, workload shaping, autoscale policies, and graceful degradation.
- Two quick clarifying questions so we bring the right folks:
  1) Is the traffic bursty (spiky) or mostly steady with diurnal changes?
  2) Any compliance constraints (SOC2, IP restrictions) we should prepare for?

Availability: I can host slots tomorrow (Wed) 11:00–12:30 PT or Thu 09:00–11:00 PT. If neither works, share a couple of windows and I can loop in Ben (AE) and Priyom (solutions engineer).

If helpful I can send a draft agenda: capacity targets, kernel/quantization choices, autoscale & fallback, observability checklist, and next steps for a pilot.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
SDR — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@sequencelabs.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interested in Dedicated capacity demo (high QPS/low latency)

Hi Neha — thanks for the quick reply.

Answers:
- Traffic: mostly steady (200–300 QPS sustained during business hours) with predictable hourly ramps, occasional short spikes to ~450 QPS for 2–3 minutes when a batch job finishes.
- Compliance: SOC2 is required for our procurement team.

Attendees: myself and Taylor Sato (infra lead). We prefer Wed 11:30–12:00 PT if you can do a tight 30-minute technical walkthrough; otherwise Thu morning works too.

I re-attached the traffic spreadsheet. Also, we have a short pre-sales questionnaire — we can share it if that helps your solutions team prepare.

Thanks,
Alex

Attachment: seq-capacity-specs.xlsx (updated)

Hi Alex — great to meet you over email, and thanks for the traffic outline. Priyom will join to go through kernel/quant options and reachability for SOC2 artifacts.

We can do Wed 11:30–12:00 PT for a focused technical session. I'll put together a tight agenda and share a calendar invite once you confirm the time.

Agenda (30 min):
- 5m: intros & goals
- 10m: Dedicated sizing + autoscale behavior (how we handle sustained QPS and short spikes)
- 8m: latency breakdown & optimizations (kv cache, batching, kernel selection)
- 5m: next steps (pilot, SOC2 artifacts, pricing/commits)

I also attached a short runbook we typically walk through for Dedicated pilots — it highlights what we measure and what we need from customers.

Calendar: https://calendly.com/redwood/sequence-dedicated-demo (or I can send a direct invite)

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-runbook.pdf

Could you confirm who will be the primary POC for security/procurement so we can pre-stage SOC2 evidence?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
